item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: The Architects Automaton
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback.

Spoiler below

+ show block
– hide block

The reason why It's vague is that it is a mystery note that develops over time. I have to decide between balancing what to say here and what not to spoil in what is effectively the general outline of the story. The problem is that anyone who is actually interested in the concept enough to greenlight it would also end up being spoiled to the story in the long run. I explained in my spoiler post for Cyber exactly why it has the effects it has. It is definitely not just a simple "it drives people insane", but the exact specifics of what it is doing and why it is doing it can fill out 400 words all on it's own and is a huge part of unraveling the mystery that I don't just want to spoil for readers.

In which care, should I care about that at all and just spill everything out?

My ultimate point is already written out as it pertains to the SPC's themselves.
But spoilers kill a story, so I'm not really sure what to do here.
And in my honest opinion, as it pertains to the mystery, I have already said too much in an effort to get greenlit for a sandbox that can't be justified in merely 400 words, but rather should be justified by the reading of the draft article itself.

is the real problem for a story… I would suggest thinking of some other effect seeing the patterns does…

Not a problem at all, because its effects are not random in the slightest and it is not merely just "driving someone insane". The idea here is that everything psychological that seems to be random is actually simply the extreme of things that already exist in the subjects, even in tiny quantities. The idea here is to put on a display that everyone, EVERYONE has some tiny piece of their mind that is not quite right, no matter how small. These patterns have hidden within them traps that latch on and exploit these small problems and cause them to grow to extremes, all in an effort to protect its creator's knowledge. Basically, the machine's patterns are not driving you insane or causing devastating mental diseases, they are simply magnifying the issues that are already there. The idea is that everyone, EVERYONE has some mental issue somewhere, no matter how small they may be. If that's not different enough of a tone then I don't really know what to say there. I'll take it back to the drawing board.

why make people crazy? What else could be done to make it unsettling?

I noted that in the spoiler for Cyber, but that is really the question here. WHY is it doing what it is doing? And the answer is written, but hidden from view because that answer literally answers the mystery of the entire object. I'll probably rewrite or update the greenlight with some spoiler sections explaining the actual story at hand, so that people can read and avoid the context should they care to read along once the story is actually unfolding as an SCP, interviews and experiment logs.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: The Architects Automaton
item.content:encoded:
It is not yet known what happens when SCP-XXXX is allowed to finish one of its patterns, but it is certainly best left to conjecture.

Why? No need to be vague when trying to sell your idea

This is by no means something that could be elevator pitched, to say the least, and yes it will be incredibly difficult to achieve.

And yet, this is what is required for greenlighting. I would suggest you streamline the idea and give us the overall points/plot and themes you're going for.

  • Instead of listing out possible other things connected to this skip, focus on selling us why we would want to read about it. What are the stakes? What is the narrative? Even cosmic horror is dependent on an arc. Yes you can be vague and hinty in the article, but here you're meant to sell the idea.
  • things that make you go crazy are a) boring, because it was done to death, and b) sorta demeaning to those who have atypical neuro states. But a) is the real problem for a story… I would suggest thinking of some other effect seeing the patterns does… The unbearable information driving someone crazy has been old news since the 1920s. Stretch your imagination, this automaton could make designs that could do anything… why make people crazy? What else could be done to make it unsettling?

I suggest you take a good look at your ultimate point, and spell it out clearly in the idea post. You can edit it by clicking on options in the post and then edit.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: The Architects Automaton
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback and criticism, and I would like to discuss this whole affair further.

The real problem here is that there is just not enough space to tell this story in under 400 words, as an elevator pitch. This is an extremely complex story that consists of multiple SCP stories all weaving into the actual narrative.

*SPOILER ALERT BELOW!*

+ show block
– hide block

To be clear: it activates if the crank is turned and not just if you like, ask it via particular audio frequencies? If so, what does 'will respond to' mean?

If audio frequencies are played for it, it will activate remotely.

Not really a fan of this angle. It feels too much like you're just throwing out a bunch of vague ideas you find kinda interesting in an attempt to make the position of the Architect more interesting, but it doesn't really and it doesn't really come across as interesting to me. More to the point, I'm not really sure how the Foundation figure out the Architect exists or like, what that actually means for this SCP or the world at large?

Generally I'm not a fan of things that just make you go crazy, particularly in a way that causes you to forget a lot; since like…it's super overplayed and often feels…kinda problematic and like it stigmatizes mental illness more. More to the point, it's also an effect that's really hard to convey in an interesting way within the confines of a SCP article.

Well… That's kind of the point really. It's a mystery that will begin to unravel with each new artifact that is found. At the stage of the automaton, the architect is nothing more than what seems to be collaborative delusion or effect of the psychosis caused by the very intentional hiding of his magic through psychological means. Think of them as a sort of trap card to hide his magic from prying eyes, which is actually a method for creating dimensional gates that he has lost. while it seems to be almost a chaotic effect at the surface, further investigations will note that it is not simply randomly causing mental illnesses, but rather the mathematical sequences hidden within its geometry are causing unknown preexisting conditions within subjects to rapidly grow in strength and effect. So someone who originally would have gotten Alzheimer's in their late 70's or 80's rapidly advances to first stage Alzheimer's within a few days. When the defense can't find a logical disease to latch onto, it instead creates a feedback effect upon a particular psychological mindset and amplifies it to extremes, like Pyromania or Schizophrenia. It is less creating effects at random and more amplifying what is already there in the mind in an active attempt to hide secrets. This can be made aware through research and the existence of the architect will be made aware of through interviews of isolated test subject interviews. the most important of which being that while researching and experimenting on the SCP and its products, two things are noted. One, that the images it produces are actually small pieces of larger puzzles that are meant to create literal dimensional gateways, and two, that the mathematically created "psychological traps" seem to have no effect on subjects who suffer from high functioning autism, which gives them the ability to compartmentalize the traps and seemingly avoid them as they put together the pieces of this massive puzzle.

While there is a story intended here, most of it will be displayed through experiment procedures and interviews, but do keep in mind that cosmic horror is a specific type of horror, and not all the answers can or will be explained fully. I feel bad even explaining this outright to you as it's more meant to be pieced together through the story of the artifacts and interviews. The lack of cohesion is very intentional because it is a mystery that will be slowly put together as the story unfolds. Though it's effects and its physical being seem to be completely disconnected from one another, they are very much connected to one another. It will just take a certain type of person to be the key to unlock the mystery.

And the story I have in mind certainly cannot be told in under 400 words on a pitch. This is by no means something that could be elevator pitched, to say the least, and yes it will be incredibly difficult to achieve. But that's partially the reason I am doing it.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: The Architects Automaton
item.content:encoded:
An Automaton of unknown origin, inexplicably in operational condition. Creates increasingly complex geometric patterns that grab the eye and boggle the mind.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Cosmic Horror mystery

Elevator Pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a functional Automaton, appearing to be from the 1800s. It resembles a small child writing at a desk, to which it is attached. Upon supplying SCP-XXXX with paper and ink for the attached pen and turning the crank, the crank will lock in place. However, it has been discovered through intense physical manipulation and scientific reasoning, that SCP-XXXX will respond to particular audio frequencies, all of which are outside the audible spectrum. It will then activate autonomously and begin drawing with extreme precision until its internal potential energy is exhausted.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
The story laying under the surface of this strange artifact as well as many others that will come is the story of the Architect. A person from an unknown time and place that has found a way to harness mathematics and geometry into a form of literal magic. Though the Architect's whereabouts and physicality are yet unknown, there are many strange, otherworldly objects that lend themselves to prove his existence.

Associate SCP concepts-
- The architect’s Automaton Known
- The arithmetic sigils (x3) Unknown
- The Arithmicon Unknown
- The huntsmen Unknown
- The Lead Knights Unknown
- The Tide Unknown
- The face of god Unknown
- The seed of Eden Unknown
- The black moor Unknown
- The eye of Yog Unknown
- The traveler's cube Unknown

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The drawings it produces vary wildly dependent on the frequency given to it and will grow in complexity with each subsequent process. It has been noted that attempting to investigate and calculate these geometric patterns will result in Dissociative Amnesia, Psychosis, Dementia, Alzheimer's syndrome, and many other effects. This is seemingly at random, and no two cases are alike but in one distinct factor. Each of the subjects exposed to the drawings seems to experience delusions and dreams of a masked figure cloaked in black.

Additional Notes:
It is not yet known what happens when SCP-XXXX is allowed to finish one of its patterns, but it is certainly best left to conjecture.
